text: Artificial intelligence is changing how we create art, music, and writing. With simple prompts, anyone can now generate a painting in seconds or compose a tune without knowing music theory. These tools are impressive and fun, but they also raise a big question: is this real creativity? Human creativity comes from personal experience, emotion, and struggle. When we write a poem, we share a piece of our soul. Machines, however, mix patterns from existing data. They can imitate style perfectly, but they don't feel joy or pain. So, rather than replacing us, AI works best as a partner—it can suggest new ideas or handle boring tasks, leaving us more time to dream. The magic may still lie in the human touch, but the future of art is certainly more open to everyone.
